cards.text: This psalm doesn't name its writer, so we'll call him the psalmist, and he is talking straight to the LORD. No "Hey, hope this finds You well." He opens with, "O LORD, God of vengeance, O God of vengeance, shine forth," and asks the Judge of the earth to rise up and render a reward to the proud.

cards.question: The proud are out there doing their thing, and the psalmist has a question for the LORD. He asks it twice. What is it?

answers.text: How long will the wicked exult
Why have You hidden Your face
Who can stand before Your anger

cards.text: And the wicked are NOT keeping it quiet: they pour out arrogant words, and all workers of iniquity boast. That's the guy who hits reply-all on the whole company to announce he got his own parking spot.

cards.question: It's not just talk, either. The psalmist tells the LORD that the wicked crush His ___.
The psalmist names who the wicked kill and murder. Who is on his list?

answers.text: Widows and foreigners and the fatherless

cards.text: So how do the wicked figure they're getting away with all this? Oh, friend. They've got a THEORY.

cards.question: True or false: the wicked say the LORD, the God of Jacob, sees everything they do.

cards.text: Now the psalmist turns and calls out: "Take notice, O senseless among the people! O fools, when will you be wise?" Ooh. Pull up a chair, this is about to get GOOD.

cards.question: The wicked say the LORD can't see. The psalmist fires back: He who affixed the ___, can He not hear? He who formed the ___, can He not see?

cards.text: He keeps going: "He who admonishes the nations, does He not discipline?" That's like telling me I don't know what's in my own cookie, when I put in every chocolate chip BY HAND. Well. By mustache.

cards.question: True or false: the psalmist says the LORD, who admonishes the nations and teaches man, lacks knowledge.
The psalmist says the LORD knows the thoughts of man. What does he say those thoughts are?

cards.text: Now the psalmist turns from the fools and talks to the LORD again. And he says somebody out there is blessed.

cards.question: Who does the psalmist call blessed?

answers.text: The man the LORD disciplines and teaches
The man who never faces any trouble
The man who pays the wicked back

cards.question: Why does the LORD discipline this man and teach him from His law?

answers.text: To grant him relief from days of trouble
To make him rich in the land
To set him over the nations

cards.text: That relief lasts until a pit is dug for the wicked. They've been bragging this WHOLE psalm, and not once did they look down to check where they're walking.

cards.question: The wicked crush God's people, but the psalmist is sure of this: the LORD will not ___ His people.

cards.text: And he's sure of this too: "Surely judgment will again be righteous, and all the upright in heart will follow it."

Then he asks, "Who will rise up for me against the wicked? Who will stand for me against the workers of iniquity?" That's you on the side of the highway with a flat tire, scrolling your contacts going, who's coming? ANYBODY?

cards.question: True or false: the psalmist says nobody helped him, so he ended up dwelling in the abode of silence.
When the psalmist says his foot is slipping, the LORD's loving devotion ___ him.

cards.text: Then he gets real honest about anxiety. I know that one, friend: back in the junk drawer, every time it rattled open, all of us held our breath.

cards.question: When anxiety overwhelms the psalmist, what does he say delights his soul?

cards.text: Then he asks the LORD whether a corrupt throne, one devising mischief by decree, could ever be His ally. Mischief by DECREE. That's mischief with paperwork. Signed. Stamped. Filed.

cards.question: The psalmist says the wicked band together against the righteous and condemn the ___ to death.
The wicked are ganging up on the righteous. What does the psalmist say the LORD has been to him?

cards.text: The psalm opened by calling on the Judge of the earth to rise up. Now it closes with what the LORD will do to the wicked.

cards.question: True or false: the psalmist says the LORD will bring the wicked's own iniquity back on them.

cards.text: He'll destroy them for their wickedness, and the psalmist says it again, plain as day: "The LORD our God will destroy them." All that bragging, and the Judge of the earth gets the last word.

findings.problem: The story card runs to three sentences: "So how do the wicked figure they're getting away with all this?" / "Oh, friend." / "They've got a THEORY."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't match the line it follows. The card quotes the admonish/discipline line, but the comparison ("telling me I don't know what's in my own cookie") is about knowledge. That is the second half of verse 10, which this card doesn't tell.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The cookie joke (someone wrongly saying Papa Dorin doesn't know what's in his own cookie) gives away the answer to card 11, which asks whether the psalmist says the LORD lacks knowledge.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
